subject: Covariate modelling with rare species - error

messages.author: a94bf563bce55f38
messages.subject: Covariate modelling with rare species - error
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to apply the recent vignette on Covariate modeling with rare species to my own data. It all works well until the last step, which is the one that generates the species specific density estimates.

When I run this:

species.ests <- dht2(ddf = all.species, 
                     flatfile = species.data,
                     strat_formula = ~Species, 
                     convert_units = convunit,
                     stratification = "object")

I get the following error:

Error in predict.ds(ddf, bigdat, compute = TRUE) : fields or factor levels in `newdata` do not match data used in fitted model

Am I using an incorrect data structure for flat file?

Thanks

Anthony

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Covariate modelling with rare species - error
parts:
Anthony

You could say you have a data structure problem  This error is a cryptic way for `dht2` to tell you that your flatfile (species.data) contains species you have filtered out when performing your detection function modelling.

Look up `droplevels()`.  That will be the solution to scrubing levels of the factor variable `Species` that are causing problems.

messages.author: effdeef071f56737
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Covariate modelling with rare species - error
parts:
Thanks Eric,

This did solve the problem. I fixed it by ensuring that the factor levels were the same for the species variables within the detection function and also the abundance estimate function `dht2`. the other thing I had to try, given your advice, was to ensure that there was only a single strata in play when given multi-species data. This gave a working solution.

Thanks again.
Anthony
